title: Sanctioning Sinaloa Cartel Leaders and Corrupt Enablers in Baja California
summary_raw:
Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman
Press Statement


			
			


			
			
September 29, 2026
The United States is today sanctioning 21 individuals and 25 entities tied to the Sinaloa Cartel, including cartel leader Ismael Zambada Sicairos (“Mayito Flaco”) and the network of Tijuana- and Mexicali-based cell leaders, financial facilitators, and corrupt Mexican officials who enable the cartel to operate with impunity along the U.S.-Mexico border.
This action underscores the Trump Administration’s commitment to dismantling the Sinaloa Cartel’s operational and political infrastructure in Mexico, disrupting the networks that fuel fentanyl trafficking, violence, and corruption, and threaten communities on both sides of the border. Today’s designations reflect the whole-of-government approach the United States is taking to combat transnational criminal organizations and the Foreign Terrorist Organizations with which they intersect.
Today’s designations highlight the corrosive reach of cartel influence into Mexican governance, particularly in Baja California, where associates of the governor’s ex-husband, a former Mexicali public security director, and other political operators allegedly accepted bribes to shield Sinaloa Cartel operations from law enforcement.
To accelerate the removal of key cartel figures from the region, the Department of State’s Narcotics Rewards Program is offering up to $5 million each for information leading to the arrest and/or conviction of Tijuana plaza bosses Alfonso Arzate Garcia (“Aquiles”) and Rene Arzate Garcia (“La Rana”), as well as up to $5 million for information leading to the arrest and/or conviction of Mexicali cartel leader Juan Jose Ponce Felix (“El Ruso”).
The action was taken pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 14059, which targets the international proliferation of illicit drugs and their means of production, and pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended by E.O. 13886, which targets terrorists and their supporters. For more information about today’s designations, please see Treasury’s press release.

source_name: U.S. Department of State - Press Releases
title: Secretary of State Marco Rubio At President Trump’s America.gov Event
summary_raw:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
Washington, D.C.
Remarks


			
			


			
			
September 29, 2026

SECRETARY RUBIO:  Thank you.  That was actually pretty amazing there by Dr. Oz.  That actually was remarkable.  This is – this is really going to be a revolution in the way that government works for the average American.  So just think about for a moment what you just saw.  They took something that millions of Americans deal with every single day, and they made it simpler and they made it easier and they made it more effective, and they made it that way in every possible way.  And that’s just one piece of the whole that we’re here to talk about today. 
So earlier this year, Joe came to my office and he showed me America.gov.  It’s a whole-of-government project.  And it touches on every department, every agency, every bureau you can imagine.  And in each and every case, the goal is simple.  It’s to make life better and easier for normal Americans.  So, you’ve already heard a few examples already. 
Now, for us at the State Department, one particular thing came to mind: the passport.  Today, more than half of Americans have one, and it has come a long way since the early days of this country.  Let me show you – this is what it looked like in 1781, just a piece of paper.  It’s a very nice one, but just a piece of paper.  And then in time, that piece of paper became a booklet.  That booklet then introduced a photograph.  And then we entered the computer age with electronic chips.  From the wax seal to the electronic chip, the American passport has become the most trusted and powerful – and I would argue most important – identity document in the entire world. 
But the document kept evolving.  Unfortunately, the process of getting one did not continue to evolve.  So today, if you need your first passport, you start at the State Department’s website, and this is what greets you.  This is what greets you.  It’s not bad.  There’s a lot of information up there, but it’s – but if you actually want to apply, that is where the maze starts.  So you have to know which form to print, you have to schedule an appointment, then you have to go wait in line, and then when something – and when something is this hard, then someone is bound to make money off of it, right? 
So today, there’s an entire cottage industry that’s built around cashing in on every stage of the passport process.  And some of these sites are charging you for forms that are free; some are charging you for appointments that are free.  And after they take your money, they take your most sensitive personal information too.  And if you make it through all of that, sometime in the future, you get this in the mail.  This is what arrives, and that’s not really the kind of packaging you would expect for the most powerful identity document you will ever receive.  We ship tens of millions of these envelopes every year. 
Now, a United States passport, it means something, right?  It’s a physical symbol of who we are.  It’s a promise that, wherever you go in the world as an American, you are one of us.  And so, I think – I think you would agree – that American citizens deserve better than this.  And that’s why the State Department is partnering with America.gov to rebuild the entire thing from the ground up, and it begins with something pretty remarkable. 
Starting next year, Americans will be able to apply for their first passport entirely online.  (Applause.) 
Let me show you how easy it is.  You would ask:  How do I apply for my first passport?  And once I’m signed-in with login.gov, I can securely see the information that the government already has about me in its system.  I don’t have to type the same thing over and over and over again. 
Now the fun part, the photo.  You can take a new one of them yourself on the phone.  You probably can’t use those filters to make you look 50 years younger, but you can take a picture of yourself on the phone in the comfort of your own home, or you can upload one directly from your own device.  You’re not going any longer to some drugstore to get your picture taken behind a white screen.  And this is a really cool feature:  You can see your photo in the context of the finished passport.  And if you don’t like it – and as you probably know, many people don’t like it, so you’re going to take 150 of these.  (Laughter.)  But eventually, you will like one.  And you can retake it until it’s the perfect shot, the one you like. 
Now, I have to say, this may be the most beautiful government checkout I’ve ever seen.  And because I’m securely logged in through login.gov, my name, my address – they’re already here.  I enter my payment securely.  So, let’s check out.  And that’s it.  There, your payment is complete, my first application.  (Applause.) 
No printing forms, no drugstore hostage photo – (laughter) – no appointment, no line, no middleman that you’re paying to do something that should be available to you.  You tell America.gov what you’re trying to do, and it walks you through every single step and tells you exactly what comes next.
And then there’s this – real-time status.  So, for years, you could track any delivery – a pizza, whatever – more precisely than you can track where your passport is in the mail.  Not anymore.  We have an estimated delivery date, so you know it’s coming. 
And by the end of 2027, our goal is for the vast majority of Americans to be able to apply for a passport or a passport card on America.gov.  Because the point of all of this, we’re doing here today – and this is simple – make the process more accessible and easier for Americans.  So, whether you live in the middle of a major city or you live in a rural town, you’ll be able to apply from anywhere.
Now, there’s one more thing. 
(Video is played.)  (Applause.)
SECRETARY RUBIO:  That looks pretty good.  I actually carry these around with me now.  There it is.  It looks even better in person.  (Applause.)  This is the 2028 U.S. passport.  And the State Department worked really closely with the National Design Studio to rethink it from cover to cover.  Because a passport – think about this – a passport is more than just a travel document.  It’s an expression of the unbreakable bond between the nation and the citizen –  a bond, by the way, that doesn’t end at the water’s edge, at our borders, but one that Americans carry with them.  You carry this with you when you travel to any corner and every corner of the globe.
And so, we found one uniquely American symbol to carry that idea from beginning to end.  You see it carved into our buildings.  You see it on the ships that defended and defend our country.  You see it on our currency.  And when our founders needed a symbol of the country itself, they placed it at the center of the Great Seal.  So frankly, there was really only one choice – the American Eagle, the emblem of American strength and freedom – and it’s instantly recognizable to everyone anywhere in the world.
Now, the eagle has always been on the cover of the passport, but Joe and his team at the design studio helped us make it even better.  So now that’s the old passport, right?  That’s the new one.  The words “United States of America” are now exactly where they belong – first, right on top – and the Great Seal is larger, it’s more prominent, it’s more gold.  (Laughter.)
And when you open the book – when you open the book, the eagle takes flight.  The eagle carries you across 250 years of America.  You see it soar, right, from the eagle’s point of view, above patriots standing their ground at Lexington and past the families crossing west with everything they owned in a wagon.  The men who drove steel across a continent and two bicycle mechanics from Ohio who taught mankind how to fly.  There’s the Marines who raised our flag on Iwo Jima and all the way to the Artemis splashdown.  The entire sweep of American history from the patriots of ’76, to the pioneers setting out into the great unknown, to the astronauts who carried our flag to the moon.
It is a visual story of the greatest nation in the history of the world – a nation destined from the very beginning for extraordinary things.  And this passport won’t just carry you; it will carry that story into the world.  And because this is the – because this is one of the most secure documents in the world, there are obviously things that I can’t and won’t show you, but here’s what I can show you.  I can show you this.  Watch the eagle as you flip through the pages.  It flies.  Now, I think that’s pretty good.  (Applause.)
I can see Americans sitting at airports all over the world, like why do people keep flipping through the page?  (Laughter.)  Well, it’s a – it’s either this or some Gameboy for your kids to keep them entertained, they can flip the eagle around.  But anyway, the book itself is beautiful.  It’s incredibly secure.  It feels substantial.  And after putting this much thought into the book itself, we figured that the way it arrives at your home ought to matter, too.  The presentation, how it gets there, should matter.
So, you remember this.  I showed this to you earlier, right?  We’re not doing that anymore.  For something as important and as dignified as the United States passport, it will arrive the way you would expect it to.  This is what comes next.  (Applause.)
Now, at the State Department we’re not waiting.  We move pretty quick.  We try to move very fast.  So, we’re not waiting until 2027 to bring you something really exciting.  A passport application experience you can complete entirely from home, and in 2028 a beautiful new United States passport, carrying 250 years of America within it, and our goal is to make passports and passport cards accessible to more Americans.  Because a United States passport says something very simple, and it says that anywhere in the world.  It says, “I – I – am an American and my country stands behind me.”  American citizenship is a sacred thing, and the symbols and documents that uphold it should reflect that.  And that’s precisely what the new United States passport will do. 
So, I hope you’ll get one, and thank you for the opportunity to present this to you today.  (Applause.)  Thank you.  (Applause.)

title: United States Disrupts Iran’s Proliferation-Sensitive Efforts in Support of UN Restrictions Fact Sheet
summary_raw:
Office of the Spokesman
Fact Sheet


			
			


			
			
September 29, 2026
Today, following the one-year anniversary of the reimposition of the UN sanctions and restrictive measures on Iran, the Department of State is designating one Iran-based entity and two Russia-based entities involved in facilitating Iran’s military procurement efforts and the transport of arms and related materiel to and from Iran, including violations of the renewed UN measures.  Over the past year, the United States has worked relentlessly with partners to enforce these restrictions, imposing dozens of new sanctions, convening representatives from 40 countries to strengthen implementation, and submitting updated identifying information on sanctioned entities to support industry implementation.
Under Operation Economic Outcast, the United States is committed to disrupting the procurement efforts of Iran’s military programs and denying Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) access to assets and resources that sustain its destabilizing activities.  This action underscores the United States’ resolve to prevent Iran from reconstituting its proliferation-sensitive programs.
The U.S. Department of State’s Rewards for Justice program is authorized under 22 U.S.C. §  2708 to offer a reward for information that disrupts the financial mechanisms of the IRGC, a U.S.-designated Foreign Terrorist Organization.
All Department of State sanctions targets are being designated pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 13949, which targets certain persons with respect to the conventional arms activities of Iran.
The Department of the Treasury is concurrently designating ten entities and individuals who have procured weapons and weapons components for Iran’s Ministry of Defense and Armed Forces Logistics (MODAFL).  For more information on these actions, please see the Department of the Treasury’s press release.
Designations Pursuant to Section 1(a)(iii) of E.O. 13949  
JOINT STOCK COMPANY EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN BUREAU NAMED AFTER A.S. YAKOVLEV (YAKOVLEV) is a Russia-based aircraft manufacturer that develops and produces the Yak-130 advanced trainer fighter jet. Russia first delivered several Yak-130 aircraft to Iran in late 2023. In November 2025, Russia delivered additional equipment associated with Yak-130 combat aircraft to Iran. These were transferred to Iran aboard a U.S.-sanctioned Russian aircraft from a manufacturing facility associated with the YAKOVLEV in Irkutsk, Russia.  In December 2025, Russia delivered several shipments of additional equipment associated with Yak-130 combat aircraft equipment to Iran from the same manufacturing facility in Irkutsk, Russia, associated with YAKOVLEV.  Russia has now delivered to Iran nearly all of its reportedly 24 contracted Yak-130 aircraft.  YAKOVLEV was previously designated pursuant to E.O. 14024 on May 19, 2023.  YAKOVLEV is being designated pursuant to section 1(a)(iii) of E.O. 13949 for having engaged, or attempted to engage, in any activity that materially contributes to, or poses a risk of materially contributing to, the proliferation of arms or related materiel or items intended for military end-uses or military end-users, including any efforts to manufacture, acquire, possess, develop, transport, transfer, or use such items, by the Government of Iran (including persons owned or controlled by, or acting for or on behalf of the Government of Iran) or paramilitary organizations financially or militarily supported by the Government of Iran.
MG-FLOT LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY (MG-FLOT) is a Russia-based shipping company whose vessels transport weapons for the Russian government. In 2024, MG-FLOT vessels were involved in the transfer of close-range ballistic missiles (CRBMs) from Iran to Russia.  In late 2025, Iran delivered air defense vehicles and related materiel from Iran to Russia aboard Russian roll-on roll-off motor vessel Kompozitor Rakhmaninov.  Kompozitor Rakhmaninov is a Russian flagged vessel identified as blocked property of MG-FLOT.  On June 27, 2022, TransMorFlot LLC changed its name to MG-FLOT.  TransMorFlot LLC was previously designated pursuant to E.O. 14024 on May 8, 2022.  MG-FLOT is being designated pursuant to section 1(a)(iii) of E.O. 13949 for having engaged, or attempted to engage, in any activity that materially contributes to, or poses a risk of materially contributing to, the proliferation of arms or related materiel or items intended for military end-uses or military end-users, including any efforts to manufacture, acquire, possess, develop, transport, transfer, or use such items, by the Government of Iran (including persons owned or controlled by, or acting for or on behalf of the Government of Iran) or paramilitary organizations financially or militarily supported by the Government of Iran.
SAHA AIRLINES is an Iran-based airline affiliated with the Islamic Republic of Iran Air Force (IRIAF) and has been involved in efforts by Iran to transport arms and related materiel. SAHA AIRLINES was previously designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 on September 8, 2026.  SAHA AIRLINES is being designated pursuant to section 1(a)(iii) of E.O. 13949 for having engaged, or attempted to engage, in any activity that materially contributes to, or poses a risk of materially contributing to, the proliferation of arms or related materiel or items intended for military end-uses or military end-users, including any efforts to manufacture, acquire, possess, develop, transport, transfer, or use such items, by the Government of Iran (including persons owned or controlled by, or acting for or on behalf of the Government of Iran) or paramilitary organizations financially or militarily supported by the Government of Iran.
Sanctions Implications
As a result of today’s sanctions actions, and in accordance with E.O. 13949, all property and interests in property of the designated persons described above that are in the United States or in possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to the Department of Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC).  In addition, all entities that are owned, directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked. 
All transactions by U.S. persons or within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of designated or otherwise blocked persons are prohibited unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC or exempt.  These prohibitions include the making of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services by, to, or for the benefit of any blocked person and the receipt of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services from any such person.   
The power and integrity of U.S. government sanctions derive not only from the U.S. government’s ability to designate and add persons to the Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN) List, but also from its willingness to remove persons from the SDN List consistent with the law. 
Petitions for removal from the SDN List may be sent to: OFAC.Reconsideration@treasury.gov.  Petitioners may also refer to the Department of State’s Delisting Guidance page.
Rewards for Justice seeks information on the financial activities of the following key leaders of the IRGC Aerospace Force (IRGC-ASF), which facilitates operations, develops weapons, and procures equipment for the IRGC’s terrorist activities.
IRGC BRIGADIER GENERAL ABDOLLAH MEHRABI is chief of the IRGC-ASF Research and Self-Sufficiency Jihad Organization (SSJO), which is responsible for the analysis and development of weapons utilized to attack U.S. armed forces personnel and infrastructure in the Middle East. Mehrabi has overseen significant advances in military satellites and drone manufacturing. As co-owner of the Oje Parvaz Mado Nafar Company, a manufacturer of engines used in Iran’s Shahed-131 and Shahed-136 UAVs, Mehrabi has acquired components for the production of Iranian Shahed drones launched against the U.S. Navy’s Fifth Fleet in Bahrain.  
AHMED JA’FARABADI is a senior IRGC-ASF official who is directly involved in the organization’s operations and logistics processes.    
ALI ASGHAR NOROUZI is the chairman of the IRGC Cooperative Foundation. The foundation serves as a slush fund for the IRGC’s personnel and their business interests. In his position as a senior IRGC officer, Norouzi has played a crucial role in the transfer of funds and weapons to allied armed proxies in the Middle East.

source_name: U.S. Department of State - Press Releases
title: Secretary of State Marco Rubio With Sean Hannity of Fox News
summary_raw:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
Washington, D.C.
Interview


			
			


			
			
September 28, 2026

QUESTION:  Anyway, here with a lot more – these are important, critical times historically – Secretary of State Marco Rubio is with us.  Sir, great to have you.   
First, let’s start with this terror —  
SECRETARY RUBIO:  Thanks, Sean.  
QUESTION:  — the terror suspects, U.S. air base out of the UK.  These guys are out on bail, Mr.  Secretary.  And I want to get your initial thoughts on what you’re hearing, what you’re seeing, and how grave a threat that is.   
SECRETARY RUBIO:  Well, let me preface by saying that I have to be careful.  There’s some things I cannot say on the air for a lot of different reasons.  Suffice it to say that what happened, what almost happened, what could have happened in the UK over the weekend is a very serious situation.  It’s one that clearly involves the hands of a foreign actor.  I won’t get into great detail about that yet.  I do want to thank the authorities in the United Kingdom, who have been very cooperative, been on top of it.  I know a lot of people are disturbed by the news that some of these people have been released on bail as – some of the people are being investigated, and obviously we’re engaging with them on all of that.   
But suffice it to say that beyond that, I would argue that they’ve been very cooperative and very helpful on something that’s a very serious incident.  And I think it ties us to the reality here, and that is we are dealing with elements in the world – and in the case of Iran, for example, who have openly threatened to attack American interests globally.  We’re going to always take that very seriously; there will be repercussions for that if it ever were to happen or even attempted.  And – but what happened this weekend could have been – and was, I think – a very serious threat.  And I want to thank the UK for their cooperation and their help on it.   
There’s a lot more news that will come out on this in the days to come, but there’s only so much I can say right now at this point about it other than this is a very serious thing and it was responded to appropriately.   
QUESTION:  Mr. Secretary, let me ask you about this – and this has been a concern of mine; I’ve expressed it many times publicly.  And that is I see that Western European nations have gotten weak.  They have not committed themselves to their own security as individual countries or to NATO or even their own continent.  I see that they have adopted climate alarmism, they’ve adopted socialism, and maybe worst of all, unfettered illegal immigration without assimilation.  I never thought, sir, in my lifetime I’d see as many as 100 Sharia courts in Great Britain.  I never thought there’d be something called no-go zones throughout Europe, including in France.  I never thought that would happen.   
SECRETARY RUBIO:  Yeah.  Look, I mean, I think Europe faces some big challenges.  I gave a speech about that earlier this year in Munich at the Security Conference.  And so much of what we have in our country is a legacy of Europe, whether it’s our traditions, our culture, even our democracy, and many of the things that underpin it come from there.  So obviously we have a special place in our heart for Europe, and we have very strong alliances.  And not every country in Europe is the same, by the way.  There are countries in Europe that have been very forward-leaning on some of the things you just pointed to, and there are others that have not so much.  And we’ve all seen the images, for example, of what’s happening in Spain.   
The truth is this:  Whether it’s in Europe or in the Western Hemisphere, the United States or whatever it may be, no country – no country in the world that’s responsible, governed by responsible people – can allow their borders to just be open and allow anyone that wants to come in to flood in.  You can’t flood countries with migration.  This is a country that was built on immigration.  And immigration has to happen through an orderly process in which you get to decide who comes in, you know a lot about them, and you pick and choose how many people – who and how many people can come in every single year.  This is proper migration, proper immigration.   
What we have seen in the broader West and what we saw in the United States during the previous administration is an uncontrolled flood of people coming in.  It’s what – an analogy I’ve always used is:  I’m not against rain; I’m against flooding.  And that’s what I would say about immigration and mass migration.  Mass migration is terribly costly for any society.  It’s simply not sustainable over the long term.  I think countries in Europe are learning that now.  The United States learned that after four years under the Biden administration.  And I think other countries in our own hemisphere are dealing with some of this as well.   
QUESTION:  Mr. Secretary, you’ve been very articulate about the issue over Iran.  Every single person that I’ve interviewed that would know – and there aren’t many people that would actually know; you’re one of the people that would know.  And I’d ask everyone that did know, and they’d all give me the same answer or a version of the same answer, and that is that the President had no choice.  The President did not have a choice when it came to Midnight Hammer or Epic Fury.  And I ask you this – in light of this – is that if that is true and if everybody’s worried about the Strait of Hormuz, what would the Strait of Hormuz look like, what would the Middle East be like if Iran ever achieved their stated goal of getting nuclear weapons?   
SECRETARY RUBIO:  Yeah, so here’s what – let me take – it’s a very basic principle here.  What Iran was trying to do is they were trying to build up so many conventional weapons, meaning they’d have so many drones, so many rockets, so many missiles, that nobody could possibly touch them.  They would become immune.  And behind that shield, behind that conventional shield of weaponry to threaten the entire region, our forces, even Europe, they would then break out towards a nuclear weapon.  That was their goal.  And what the President had to address is he could not allow them to cross the line of immunity.  He could not allow them to reach a point where they had so many missiles, so many drones, and so many weapons that you couldn’t do anything militarily about their nuclear program.  That’s what they were trying to achieve.  That’s what the President prevented.  And he saved the world a tremendous amount of trouble. 
Now, look, the only way we would have found out the opposite is to allow it to happen, and then five years from now everyone would be saying:  I can’t believe they allowed Iran, behind a conventional shield, to build and develop a nuclear weapons program, and now you have North Korea in the Middle East.  That’s what we were on the verge of.  That’s what the President has prevented.  And that’s what he has consistently said from the very beginning of this operation:  Iran can never have a nuclear weapon.  And that’s what this whole endeavor has been about from the very beginning, and that’s what he’s focused on and continues to be focused on.   
If Iran had a nuclear weapon – if Iran had a nuclear weapon – they could do whatever they want with the straits.  Think about what we’re doing right now, and I think you saw a few minutes ago you were playing videos of Scott Bessent commenting on it.  The straits are opened.  There is almost as much oil flowing through the straits now as before this conflict, with the exception of Iranian oil, which is not getting out.  If Iran had a nuclear weapon with which it could threaten its neighbors and the world, no one would be able to do anything about the straits.  They would be able to control the straits, charge a toll, and decide who got energy and who did not get energy on this planet. 
That’s what they would do if they had a nuclear weapon, and worse.  We are talking about a regime that has slaughtered – slaughtered – tens, maybe hundreds of thousands of their own people throughout this so-called revolution.  If that’s what they’re willing to do to their own people, imagine what they would do to Americans or others in the region or Israelis or anybody if they had a nuclear weapon.  They have no regard for the lives of anyone else.   
And my last point I want to make about it.  Oftentimes people make the mistake of equating Iran to a country.  It is a country, but the problem with Iran is not the country.  The problem with Iran is the revolution, and that’s what governs in that country.  It’s not the government officials you see with the suits on that go on Meet the Press and get this free pass on American media.  That’s not who we’re talking about here.  Who calls the shots in Iran are radical Shia clerics with an apocalyptic vision of the future.  They believe that it is their religious calling to trigger about the last days of the world and the apocalypse. 
I know this sounds – to a lot of people watching it, it sounds like something from a science – from a movie, but it is the reality.  It is the stated purpose of their revolution.  People like that can never possess a nuclear weapon, because they will use it to blackmail the world and to kill people.  It is an unacceptable risk, and President Trump did what other American presidents said but never did, which is prevent Iran from getting one. 
QUESTION:  Let’s go back to Scott Bessent’s comments.  He said their – the Iranians’ ability to raise cash and their ability – or they’ll have nothing left to trade in two weeks, while simultaneously the foreign minister of Iran is talking about drawing up a doomsday war scenario plan.  And look, they peddle propaganda regularly, but are we that close to seeing the Iranians bankrupt?  We know inflation is about 500 percent, half the adult workforce is out of work, and bare necessities are in very short supply.  Are they really that close to being bankrupted? 
SECRETARY RUBIO:  Yeah.  I mean, I think they are there now, and they’re heading there fast to a cataclysm.  And they’ve never been good economically.  It’s sad, by the way, because Iran is a country with tremendous potential.  Its people are incredible people, hardworking people, smart, industrious, with an ancient history to fall back on, and have achieved many things.  At one point, Iran was one of the most prosperous countries in the Middle East before the radical clerics took over, so it’s a very sad situation.  Their economy now is a cataclysm.   
But here’s the other point people don’t realize.  This is not simply about imposing economic costs on this regime.  Every dollar that Iran has, what they have done over the last 30 years is anytime they get money – be it under Obama’s sanction relief, be it under economic selling of oil and gas or whatever – they don’t use that money to build hospitals; they don’t use that money to build roads.  They don’t use that money to improve the life of the Iranian people.  They use that money to do two things: build weapons for themselves and export the revolution.  They use the money to fund Hizballah; they use the money to fund Hamas; they use the money to fund Shia militias in Iraq.  That’s what they use – they use the money to sponsor terrorism and assassination plots all over the world. 
And so every penny that they get into their hands is money that they use for purposes of these malign activities.  And so when you’re denying them money through oil sales and sanctions, you’re not just punishing them.  You are preventing them from getting access to money that they will use to try and kill Americans and others around the world and their own people, and build weapons and threaten the world and ultimately break out to a nuclear weapon program. 
QUESTION:  Let me ask you about President Xi’s visit.  Look, I’m never going to – I’m never going to trust the communist Chinese.  I don’t think most Americans will trust them.  Their intellectual property theft alone is a clear and present danger.  I really worry about those people that would want us to unilaterally disarm when it comes to artificial intelligence, for example.  The communist Chinese are not going to stop.   
But I want to ask you this.  Just prior to the visit, it was announced that the President – and I think people didn’t even take him seriously when he was talking about Greenland, but he was able to secure a deal where we can build our military bases and maintain them in perpetuity, even if the island were ever sold off, and simultaneously keeping out our top geopolitical foes, being China and Russia.  How did President Xi react to that news?   
SECRETARY RUBIO:  Well, it didn’t come up.  We didn’t discuss it in the meetings.  It didn’t come up.  But I can tell you it’s an extraordinary achievement by the President.  He hasn’t gotten nearly enough credit for it. 
From the very beginning, going back to the first administration under President Trump, but now he’s made abundantly clear that the issue of Greenland is not about territorial conquest; it is about national security.  Now, Greenland has always been important.  It was important during the Second World War, which is why the United States had to secure it during the Second World War to prevent Nazi Germany from taking it over and so forth.  It’s always played an important role during the Cold War.   
It has a more important role today than ever before for two reasons.  Number one is because the Arctic region has now become an area of incredible competition.  Multiple countries, including countries that are not Arctic countries that call themselves near-Arctic countries like China, are out there operating every single day trying to dominate sea lanes, which are important for global shipping and commerce. 
But the other is because of space warfare and because of missile defense.  In order to build the sort of missile defense this country needs to protect itself, Greenland is incredibly important for all of North America.  And so the fear was and the concern has always been – and we’ve seen this play out in other parts of the world – is that countries and potential adversaries go into a place and they use investments; they buy a port, they build a port, they build an airport, they build something that has a dual use to it.  It looks like an airport, it looks like a seaport, but it’s built in a way that looks like a military base.  And they begin to access land rights and possession rights in these places, and all of a sudden you wake up one day and you realize that you have an adversary and a competitor that’s taken control of the Panama Canal or taken control of some other critical part of the world.  And so it’s always been about national security. 
And what we were able to reach is an agreement with both the Kingdom of Norway but also Denmark that allows us now to have the presence that we need to secure it – Greenland – secure our national security and is good for them as well.  Under this agreement which exists now in perpetuity, never will any adversary of the United States have the ability to invest there without our approval and their approval, but also we will have access to building new military facilities that will allow us to build the sort of missile defense shield that all of North America needs.  It benefits North America, it benefits Europe, it benefits NATO.  So it’s an extremely – and it didn’t cost the American taxpayer a single penny.  An incredible achievement, and I think our allies are happy with it as well.
QUESTION:  Before I go to Latin America and Cuba and Venezuela, let me ask you this question:  Would we have the ability to get rare earth minerals, for example, that apparently Greenland might be very rich in?
SECRETARY RUBIO:  Sure.  We will do it in partnership with them.  I mean, at the end, I mean, this is an allied country, this is an allied place.  They now – now that this is behind us, I think we have the opportunity to make good investments there.  We’d do it in partnership with them.  It’ll be beneficial for them. 
That’s not why we did it.  I mean, the key to Greenland, as I said, is its geography is so critically important to our national security.  That’s what it’s always been about.  If there are commercial opportunities that are beneficial for us but also beneficial to Greenland, that’s something we’ll be able to explore.
What we don’t have to worry about is some adversary taking control of that and using it for their own benefit as opposed to the benefit of our allies and ultimately of the United States as well.
QUESTION:  Is Cuba about to fall, and can you update us on Venezuela?
SECRETARY RUBIO:  Well, the truth is Cuba has already fallen.  It’s not – it doesn’t have a functional economy and it’s governed by people who continue to preach about some revolution that has been dead for 20 years that’s never worked.  And that’s the problem they have.  The problem that Cuba has basically right now is that it is a failed state in every sense of the word.  Now, they may have a government that’s capable of jailing and killing people.  They have a regime that’s capable of and has jailed and killed people.  But it’s not a functional government and it’s not a functional country.  It just simply isn’t.
And in addition to that, it’s one that’s fueled by corruption, graft, and theft.  The Cuban economy – there is no Cuban economy that benefits the Cuban people.  Anything that had a chance of making money in Cuba was controlled by the Cuban military and the Cuban Communist Party to line the pockets of a handful of individuals at the expense of the entire country.  You know that since 2021 at least close to 20 percent of Cuba’s population has left the country?  Has left it because it’s a failure, a complete failure.
So we are hopeful that Cuba will choose a different path.  We are hopeful that the people that today sort of control the arms and the repressive regime, that there will be some people in there that open their eyes to the reality of what they’re facing.  What they’re no longer going to do as long as Donald Trump is President is they’re no longer going to be able to steal money and make money off the backs of the Cuban people.  And what we’re not going to allow ever under any circumstances as long as President Trump is President is we’re never going to allow Cuba to become a base of operation against American interests or pose a threat to our national security.  On that we are abundantly clear.
As in every case – you can ask about any country or any problem in the world, and I will tell you that the preference of our President is to solve these things diplomatically and in a way that you can reach an agreement and get Cuba or any country on a path to irreversible, positive change that involves economic freedoms but also involves political freedoms.  In fact, you cannot have economic freedom in Cuba if you don’t have political freedom first.  You have to have both happening at least at the same time.  That will require a period of transition.  Unfortunately, the people that continue there to chant revolutionary slogans – too many of them – still believe that they could wait out this administration and make no changes or do nothing.  They are wrong and they will learn the lesson the hard way if they don’t correct.
QUESTION:  And the partnership with Venezuela?  We have about 30 seconds.
SECRETARY RUBIO:  Well, in Venezuela two things are happening.  One, their economy needs to continue to recover because the people of Venezuela have suffered so much.  Understand we’re talking about 25 or 30 years of corruption and graft.  But the other thing that has to happen and we’re really focused on is a democratic transition.  They need to have free and fair elections in that country.  We’re working very hard with the 2015 National Assembly to put in place the conditions necessary to have free and fair elections as soon as possible, and then Venezuela will really be on the upswing it deserves to be on.
QUESTION:  All right.  Secretary of State Marco Rubio, we appreciate your time as always.  Thank you, sir.
